risks.radEduBody: Absorbed dose (mGy) and equivalent/effective dose (mSv) measure distinct physical and biological quantities and are NEVER converted into each other. NASA-STD-3001 career effective dose limit is 600 mSv (universal for age and sex); 30-day SPE reference is below 250 mSv; ISS effective dose is typically 0.2 to 0.5 mSv/day. ISS-RAD alarms for crew shelter decisions while CAD tracks personal accumulated dose and rate.

R-RAD-01.title: Absorbed Dose Rate Above Typical LEO Range
R-RAD-01.explanation: Absorbed dose rate exceeds 0.4 mGy/day, which is above the typical LEO crew badge range (< 0.3 mGy/day).
R-RAD-01.next_step: Confirm detector reading and location, compare with a second instrument if available, and record the source.

R-RAD-02.title: Radiation Dose Margin Reached 50%
R-RAD-02.explanation: Career effective dose >= 50% of 600 mSv or trailing 30-day effective dose >= 50% of 250 mSv.
R-RAD-02.next_step: Continue scheduled weekly dosimetry logging and review exposure trends with mission planning.
R-RAD-02.source: Prototype margin on NASA-STD-3001 600 mSv career / 250 mSv 30-day references

R-RAD-03.title: Radiation Dose Margin Reached 80%
R-RAD-03.explanation: Career effective dose >= 80% of 600 mSv or trailing 30-day effective dose >= 80% of 250 mSv.
R-RAD-03.next_step: Notify the Doctor and mission support; follow the mission ALARA procedures.
R-RAD-03.source: Prototype margin on NASA-STD-3001 600 mSv career / 250 mSv 30-day references

R-RAD-04.title: NASA Effective Dose Reference Reached
R-RAD-04.explanation: Career effective dose >= 600 mSv universal limit or trailing 30-day effective dose >= 250 mSv reference.
R-RAD-04.next_step: Immediately notify mission support and Flight Surgeon / Doctor; execute approved dose-limit operational procedures.
R-RAD-04.source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 (600 mSv career limit) & ISS 30-day SPE reference (250 mSv)

R-RAD-05.title: Solar Particle Event (SPE) In Progress
R-RAD-05.explanation: Commander logged Solar Event Status = SPE in progress.
R-RAD-05.next_step: Follow the mission approved solar particle event contingency procedures (shielding/shelter plan) and contact mission support.
R-RAD-05.source: NASA OCHMO TB-020 / NASA SRAG ISS-RAD Shelter Operations

R-ENV-01.title: Verified 1-Hour Average ppCO2 Exceeds 3 mmHg
R-ENV-01.explanation: Verified rolling 1-hour average (>= 5 samples, >= 60 min span, max gap <= 20 min) exceeds NASA-STD-3001 [V2 6004] 3.0 mmHg criterion.
R-ENV-01.next_step: Check ventilation and CO2 removal status on the approved vehicle displays, re-sample, notify mission support; crew reporting symptoms should contact the Doctor.

R-ENV-02.title: Single ppCO2 Sample Above 3 mmHg (Coverage Incomplete)
R-ENV-02.explanation: A single ppCO2 sample exceeds 3.0 mmHg while 1-hour sampling coverage is not yet verified.
R-ENV-02.next_step: Single sample above 3 mmHg; the one-hour average cannot be verified yet. Continue sampling every 15 minutes until coverage >= 60 minutes.

R-ENV-03.title: 7-Day Average ppCO2 Above 2.5 mmHg
R-ENV-03.explanation: 7-day mean ppCO2 exceeds 2.5 mmHg; NASA OCHMO TB-004 links keeping the 7-day average below 2.5 mmHg to <1% headache risk.
R-ENV-03.next_step: Review scrubber performance trending on approved vehicle displays and continue scheduled sampling.

R-ENV-04.title: Cabin ppO2 Outside Normoxia Target Range
R-ENV-04.explanation: Oxygen partial pressure is outside the NASA normoxia target range of 145 to 155 mmHg.
R-ENV-04.next_step: Verify the sensor reading, check atmosphere control status on vehicle displays, and notify mission support.

R-ENV-05.title: Total Pressure or Diluent Gas Outside Limits
R-ENV-05.explanation: Total cabin pressure is outside 34.5–103 kPa or diluent gas fraction is below 30%.
R-ENV-05.next_step: Immediately verify approved cabin pressure displays, inspect seals/atmosphere supply status, and notify mission support.

R-ENV-06.title: Temperature or Relative Humidity Outside Envelope
R-ENV-06.explanation: Cabin temperature/humidity is outside crew performance zone (20–25 C, 30–60% RH) or outside crew health limits (18 C/75% RH to 27 C/25% RH).
R-ENV-06.next_step: Check cabin thermal control status on approved displays, verify sensor accuracy, and notify mission support if outside health limits.

R-ENV-07.title: Cabin Ventilation Degraded or Off
R-ENV-07.explanation: Commander logged cabin ventilation status as Degraded or Off.
R-ENV-07.next_step: Confirm airflow status on approved vehicle displays, monitor ppCO2 closely, and follow mission ventilation contingency procedures.
R-ENV-07.source: Prototype operational rule / ECLSS ventilation context

R-GRV-01.title: Weekly Exercise Days Below NASA 6-Day Reference
R-GRV-01.explanation: Mission weekly exercise schedule logged fewer than 6 days against NASA ISS reference (2.5-hour blocks 6 days/week, 1 rest day).
R-GRV-01.next_step: Operational note only: review equipment availability and crew schedule flexibility without ranking or comparing individuals.

R-ISO-01.title: Extended Interval Since Last Ground Contact
R-ISO-01.explanation: More than 7 days recorded since the last scheduled ground-contact session.
R-ISO-01.next_step: Note communication cadence in mission log and verify upcoming ground-support contact schedule.
R-ISO-01.source: Prototype operational rule / Behavioral health context

R-DST-01.title: Spacecraft Communication Link Degraded
R-DST-01.explanation: Commander recorded communication link status as Degraded.
R-DST-01.next_step: Verify antenna/link telemetry and prepare offline protocols if delay or bandwidth worsens.

R-DST-02.title: Loss of Signal (Communication Link)
R-DST-02.explanation: Commander recorded Loss of Signal on the Earth-spacecraft link.
R-DST-02.next_step: Follow the mission communication-loss procedures; use locally stored protocols; ASTRA keeps working offline and queues entries.

R-HR-01.title: Resting Heart Rate Outside 60–100 bpm
R-HR-01.explanation: Resting heart rate reading is below 60 bpm or above 100 bpm (applied strictly to Resting context).
R-HR-01.next_step: Re-measure after 5 minutes of quiet rest using the same approved device, then record the repeat measurement.
R-HR-01.source: General published clinical adult resting HR reference (60–100 bpm)

R-HR-02.title: Consecutive Days Outside Resting Heart Rate Reference
R-HR-02.explanation: Two resting heart rate readings outside 60–100 bpm recorded on consecutive UTC days.
R-HR-02.next_step: Follow repeat measurement protocol and contact the designated Doctor for procedural review.

R-BP-01.title: Blood Pressure Elevated / Stage 1 Reference (>=130/80 mmHg)
R-BP-01.explanation: Systolic >= 130 mmHg or diastolic >= 80 mmHg per ACC/AHA 2017 categories.
R-BP-01.next_step: Follow BP measurement protocol (seated/relaxed 5 minutes, arm at heart level, two readings 1 minute apart) and re-record.

R-BP-02.title: Blood Pressure Stage 2 Reference (>=140/90 mmHg)
R-BP-02.explanation: Systolic >= 140 mmHg or diastolic >= 90 mmHg per ACC/AHA 2017 categories.
R-BP-02.next_step: Repeat reading after 5 minutes of quiet rest (two readings 1 minute apart) and contact the Doctor for review.

R-BP-03.title: Blood Pressure High-Priority Threshold (>180/120 mmHg)
R-BP-03.next_step: Follow BP measurement protocol immediately, repeat the reading to rule out artifact, and contact the Doctor immediately.

R-BP-04.title: Low Blood Pressure Reference (<90/60 mmHg)
R-BP-04.next_step: Repeat reading after 5 minutes of quiet rest, verify cuff placement at heart level, and notify the Doctor if persistent or symptomatic.

R-SLP-01.title: Sleep Duration Below 7.0 Hours
R-SLP-01.explanation: Recorded sleep duration is below the 7.0-hour adult consensus minimum (NASA schedules 8.5 hours).
R-SLP-01.next_step: Review rest schedule and lighting routine per mission guidelines; log upcoming sleep period on waking.
R-SLP-01.source: AASM/SRS 2015 Consensus Statement & NASA-STD-3001 (8.5 h schedule)

R-SLP-02.title: Three Consecutive Nights Below 7.0 Hours
R-SLP-02.explanation: Three consecutive sleep entries are below 7.0 hours.
R-SLP-02.next_step: Doctor notified for procedural schedule review. Continue recording morning sleep hours.
R-SLP-02.source: Prototype consecutive-night rule on AASM/SRS 7.0 h threshold

R-SLP-03.title: Downward Sleep Duration Trend (>=3 Decreasing Steps)
R-SLP-03.explanation: Three or more consecutive decreasing sleep duration steps detected across stored nights.
R-SLP-03.next_step: Informational trend notice: continue logging daily sleep duration upon waking.

R-MOOD-01.title: Consecutive Very Low Self-Reported Mood
R-MOOD-01.explanation: Mood level 1 (Very low) recorded on two consecutive entries. Shared privately with Doctor only.
R-MOOD-01.next_step: Private Doctor check-in recommended per mission behavioral health procedures.

R-STR-01.title: Elevated Daily Stress Rating (>=70/100)
R-STR-01.explanation: Daily stress self-rating reached 70/100 or higher. Shared privately with Doctor only.
R-STR-01.next_step: Note operational workload context and repeat scheduled daily self-check.

R-STR-02.title: Three Consecutive Days of Stress >= 70/100
R-STR-02.explanation: Self-reported stress >= 70/100 on three consecutive entries. Shared privately with Doctor only.
R-STR-02.next_step: Doctor notified privately for confidential procedural support review.

R-ACT-01.title: Weekly Exercise Below NASA Reference Schedule
R-ACT-01.explanation: Logged exercise days this week are fewer than the NASA ISS reference of 6 days/week (1.5 h resistive + 1 h aerobic).
R-ACT-01.next_step: Neutral operational note only (rest days are part of the reference); log completed sessions.

R-DATA-01.title: Two Consecutive Days Without Daily Entries
R-DATA-01.explanation: Crew member has two consecutive UTC days with no daily health entries.
R-DATA-01.next_step: Verify device sync or connectivity status and resume scheduled daily logging.

R-DATA-02.title: Weekly Hazard Entry Overdue
R-DATA-02.explanation: Weekly mission hazard assessment is overdue by 1 day or more.
R-DATA-02.next_step: Open Mission Risks or Calendar to enter the weekly Commander hazard log with instrument & UTC timestamp.

R-REP-01.title: Crew Problem Report Submitted
R-REP-01.explanation: A crew member submitted a manual problem report for Doctor review.
R-REP-01.next_step: Doctor reviews the verbatim report text and contacts the crew member via approved mission channels.

PRT-HR.title: Resting Heart Rate Protocol
PRT-HR.purpose: Capture standardized resting heart rate with context and approved instrument.
PRT-HR.safety: Prototype default protocol. Adapt to the devices and procedures approved for your mission.
PRT-HR.step1: Sit or float quietly relaxed for 5 minutes before measurement.
PRT-HR.step2: Use the approved crew medical device or wearable.
PRT-HR.step3: Record beats per minute (bpm) and select context (Resting / After exercise / Other).
PRT-HR.step4: Verify and record the UTC measurement timestamp.

PRT-BP.title: Blood Pressure Protocol
PRT-BP.purpose: Measure systolic and diastolic blood pressure under standardized resting conditions.
PRT-BP.safety: Prototype default protocol. Adapt to the devices and procedures approved for your mission.
PRT-BP.step1: Rest quietly for 5 minutes before taking a reading.
PRT-BP.step2: Keep the cuffed arm supported at heart level.
PRT-BP.step3: Take two readings 1 minute apart and record the average or confirmed values.
PRT-BP.step4: Note the approved device ID and UTC measurement time.

PRT-SLP.title: Morning Sleep Duration Log
PRT-SLP.purpose: Log total nightly sleep duration upon waking (NASA schedules 8.5 h; adult consensus >= 7 h).
PRT-SLP.safety: Prototype default protocol. Adapt to the devices and procedures approved for your mission.
PRT-SLP.step1: Record total sleep hours shortly after waking.
PRT-SLP.step2: Optionally record sleep start and end UTC times and source.

PRT-MOOD.title: Daily Mood Self-Check
PRT-MOOD.purpose: Private self-report check-in (never shared with Commander or compared between crew).
PRT-MOOD.safety: Prototype default protocol. Adapt to the devices and procedures approved for your mission.
PRT-MOOD.step1: Select the 1–5 mood level that best fits today (1 = Very low, 5 = Very good).
PRT-MOOD.step2: Confirm UTC timestamp; entry remains strictly private.

PRT-STR.title: Daily Stress Rating
PRT-STR.safety: Prototype default protocol. Adapt to the devices and procedures approved for your mission.
PRT-STR.step1: Enter a 0 to 100 self-rating reflecting current perceived stress.
PRT-STR.step2: Confirm UTC timestamp; entry stays private to you and the Doctor.

PRT-ACT.title: Countermeasure Exercise Log
PRT-ACT.purpose: Log exercise sessions against the NASA ISS 2.5 h/day, 6 days/week countermeasure schedule.
PRT-ACT.safety: Prototype default protocol. Adapt to the devices and procedures approved for your mission.
PRT-ACT.step1: Select session type (Resistive / Aerobic / Other) and duration in minutes.
PRT-ACT.step2: Mark completion status and record UTC timestamp.

PRT-RAD.title: Weekly Radiation Dosimetry Protocol
PRT-RAD.purpose: Record absorbed (mGy) and effective (mSv) radiation doses separately from approved dosimeters.
PRT-RAD.safety: Prototype default protocol. Adapt to the devices and procedures approved for your mission.
PRT-RAD.step1: Read total mission dose and recent dose rate from CAD and active monitor (ISS-RAD or equivalent).
PRT-RAD.step2: Enter absorbed dose (mGy) and effective dose (mSv) in separate fields without conversion.
PRT-RAD.step3: Note detector location/module, solar particle event status, and UTC timestamps.

PRT-ENV.title: Weekly Cabin Atmosphere Sampling Protocol
PRT-ENV.purpose: Verify 1-hour rolling ppCO2 average (>=5 samples, >=60 min span, max gap <=20 min) plus ppO2, pressure, temp/RH.
PRT-ENV.safety: Prototype default protocol. Adapt to the devices and procedures approved for your mission.
PRT-ENV.step1: Take ppCO2 readings every 15 minutes over at least 75 minutes (minimum 5 samples spanning >= 60 minutes).
PRT-ENV.step2: Enter ppO2 (mmHg), total pressure (kPa), diluent %, temperature (C), RH %, and ventilation status.

PRT-GRV.title: Weekly Altered Gravity & Countermeasure Review
PRT-GRV.purpose: Log mission gravity state and weekly exercise countermeasure day counts.
PRT-GRV.safety: Prototype default protocol. Adapt to the devices and procedures approved for your mission.
PRT-GRV.step1: Record current gravity environment (e.g., Microgravity, Lunar 0.165g, Mars 0.38g).
PRT-GRV.step2: Enter weekly scheduled exercise days completed (target 6 days/week with 1 rest day).

PRT-ISO.title: Weekly Isolation & Ground Contact Log
PRT-ISO.purpose: Track ground-contact sessions and aggregate crew check-in participation without exposing individual psych data.
PRT-ISO.safety: Prototype default protocol. Adapt to the devices and procedures approved for your mission.
PRT-ISO.step1: Record number of ground-contact sessions completed this week.
PRT-ISO.step2: Record days elapsed since last successful ground contact.

PRT-DST.title: Weekly Distance & Communication Link Status
PRT-DST.purpose: Update spacecraft Earth distance (km) and link status to compute one-way and round-trip light time.
PRT-DST.safety: Prototype default protocol. Adapt to the devices and procedures approved for your mission.
PRT-DST.step1: Read spacecraft-Earth distance (km) from Mission control uplink or Onboard navigation display.
PRT-DST.step2: Record current communication status (Nominal / Degraded / Loss of signal).

edu_radiation.title: Radiation Awareness
edu_radiation.summary: NASA-STD-3001 establishes a universal 600 mSv career effective dose limit across age and sex, and ISS operations reference < 250 mSv 30-day limits for Solar Particle Events (SPE). Typical ISS effective dose is 0.2 to 0.5 mSv/day, while crew badge absorbed dose is usually below 0.3 mGy/day. Absorbed dose (Gy/mGy) and effective dose (Sv/mSv) measure different quantities and are never converted into each other. ISS-RAD alarms for crew shelter decisions, while CAD tracks personal mission dose and rate.

q1.prompt: What is NASA's universal career effective dose limit under NASA-STD-3001?
q1.exp: NASA-STD-3001 sets a universal 600 mSv career effective dose limit independent of age and sex.

q2.prompt: Should absorbed dose (mGy) and effective dose (mSv) be converted into each other in ASTRA?
q2.opt0: No — they measure distinct physical and biological quantities and stay separate.
q2.opt1: Yes — multiply mGy by 10 to obtain mSv.
q2.opt2: Only during a Solar Particle Event.
q2.exp: Gy/mGy (absorbed) and Sv/mSv (effective/equivalent) depend on radiation weighting factors and are always kept separate.

q3.prompt: Which instrument primarily serves an alarm role for crew shelter decisions?
q3.exp: ISS-RAD is an active detector with an alarm role for SPE shelter decisions and trending.

edu_sleep.title: Sleep Education
edu_sleep.summary: NASA schedules an 8.5-hour sleep period for crew members, while the AASM/SRS 2015 consensus recommends adults regularly sleep at least 7 hours per night. In LEO, stations experience roughly 16 sunrises and sunsets per day, so spacecraft lighting systems simulate a 24-hour day-night cycle and consistent routines support alertness and cognition.

q1.prompt: What is the minimum nightly sleep recommended for adults by AASM/SRS 2015?
q1.exp: AASM/SRS 2015 recommends 7 or more hours per night on a regular basis (while NASA schedules an 8.5 h period).

q2.prompt: Approximately how many sunrises and sunsets does a LEO ISS-class station see each day?
q2.exp: At ~92 minutes per orbit, LEO stations experience ~16 sunrises/sunsets per 24-hour UTC day.

q3.prompt: How long is NASA's scheduled daily sleep period?
q3.exp: NASA schedules an 8.5-hour sleep period for crew members.

edu_exercise.title: Exercise Protocol Learning
edu_exercise.summary: Per NASA NTRS 20110016265, ISS countermeasure exercise blocks are scheduled for 2.5 hours per day, 6 days per week (1.5 hours resistive + 1.0 hour aerobic, with 1 scheduled rest day). This routine helps protect muscle mass, bone density, and aerobic capacity in microgravity.

q1.prompt: How many days per week is the ISS countermeasure exercise block scheduled, including rest days?
q1.exp: NASA ISS countermeasure reference schedules 6 days/week with 1 planned rest day.

q2.prompt: What is the reference daily countermeasure breakdown?
q2.opt0: 1.5 hours resistive + 1.0 hour aerobic (2.5 hours total)
q2.exp: The reference block totals 2.5 hours/day: 1.5 h resistive plus 1 h aerobic exercise.

q3.prompt: Does ASTRA penalize crew points for rest days or deferrals?
q3.opt1: Yes, rest days trigger a commander alert.
q3.opt2: No — rest days and deferrals are never penalized.
q3.exp: ASTRA prototype points never penalize rest days, deferrals, or health/exercise values.

edu_readiness.title: Mission Readiness Learning
edu_readiness.summary: Station crew schedules align on UTC/GMT (wake near 06:00 GMT, scheduled sleep 8.5 h). Environmental guidelines target normoxia ppO2 between 145 and 155 mmHg and verify 1-hour rolling ppCO2 <= 3.0 mmHg [V2 6004]. Signal light-time delay reaches ~1.28 s one-way at the Moon (384,400 km) and roughly 3 to 22 minutes one-way during Mars missions.

q1.prompt: What is the NASA [V2 6004] 1-hour average ppCO2 criterion threshold?
q1.exp: NASA-STD-3001 [V2 6004] triggers an alert when a verified 1-hour average ppCO2 exceeds 3.0 mmHg.

q2.prompt: What is the approximate one-way light time between Earth and the Moon (~384,400 km)?
q2.exp: 384,400 km / 299,792.458 km/s is approximately 1.28 seconds one-way (~2.56 s round trip).

q3.prompt: What is NASA's normoxia target range for cabin ppO2 [V2 6003]?
q3.exp: NASA-STD-3001 [V2 6003] specifies a normoxia ppO2 target window of 145 to 155 mmHg.
